Determinism and ordering guarantees** (`HOST` mode, same build and platform). **G1 Order**: commands apply in ascending `(queued_tick, host_order)`; in single-player that is submission order. *Carve-out (paused service cycle, CR-2)*: commits there are ordered by the same key but at the frozen `T`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **G2 Single timeline**: every command applies at exactly one tick (a paused-cycle commit applies at the current, frozen `T`; running-tick commands satisfy `apply_tick ≥ queued_tick + 1`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **G3 Replay**: from an initial snapshot, the same `PLAYER` command stream, the same *recorded physics observations* and the same **control-plane request log** (each request with the boundary at which it was honoured, including any paused cycle's `host_order` keys, the `restore_epoch` each restore or new game installed, and every accepted or refused runtime `set_knob` change with its boundary) yield identical block state at tick N (canonical snapshot hash), **given `(save bytes, restore_epoch)`**: the same pair replays identically and a different epoch changes exactly the epoch-keyed threat streams (D.10) and nothing else *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)*. **The log's format and owner**: the kernel emits one diagnostic *request event* per control-plane request and per admitted `PLAYER` command `(kind, boundary = (T, phase or frame-boundary), host_order, payload digest)`; a **test-side recorder** subscribed as `DIAGNOSTIC` collects them into the replay stream. The `COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY` ring buffer is a diagnostics aid with eviction and is **not** the replay source *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **G4 Save equivalence**: snapshot at T, restore, continue ≡ uninterrupted play for `persist` blocks (hash-compared) — the key regression test for CR-8. *Preconditions*: (1) every `SYSTEM`-submitting hook obeys the CR-9 owner rule (the pending queue is not saved, so a `SYSTEM` command queued at tick T's P3 is absent after a restore at T; a restart-safe hook resubmits from state); (2) **no `PLAYER` command is pending at the capture boundary** — pending commands are not in the snapshot and are `Dropped(RELOAD)` by the restore, so a capture with a non-empty queue is not equivalent to uninterrupted play; the harness captures at a boundary where the queue has drained (it submits nothing on the preceding tick), and the **remaining command stream** is then defined as the recorded `PLAYER` commands admitted **after** that boundary, fed to both runs; (3) the restored run and the control run use the **same `restore_epoch`** (tests pin it; the control run's epoch is the one the restored run was given), because a different epoch deliberately changes threat draws *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review, delegated ruling R1)*. **Cross-platform note**: G1–G4 are guaranteed on the same build and platform only; a save written on another platform or build that reports `match = false` in the K-4 verdict is expected where any `SIM` state is float-valued, not a kernel defect, and Save/Load's REBASED policy must treat it so *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **G5** exactly-one-result (CR-5). **G6 Atomic ticks** (CR-2). Physics-derived facts (positions after collision, contacts, raycasts) are *inputs* from the engine: Godot Physics 2D makes no determinism claim, so G3 either records and replays them or excludes physics-coupled blocks. This is a stated limit, not a defect; host-authoritative co-op needs host truth, not cross-machine lockstep. In the MVP no block is physics-coupled: Body's `body.integrate` hook integrates ship-local integer kinematics and samples nothing (the avatar has no physics body), so G3 needs no recorded observations and Open Question 5 is moot for the MVP *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics (BDY-3))*. → ADR
140	
141	**CR-14. Hard rules** — each becomes a lint, a test, or a control-manifest line. **H1** No domain state in the kernel (kernel-owned data is exactly: `kernel.clock`, the command queue, the registries, the binding tables, the command log, kernel state, diagnostics). **H2** No kernel-defined domain commands; its control plane (CR-15) is a host-local API, not commands. **H3** One owner per block; writes only via owner mutators inside a `WriteScope`. **H4** Presentation never writes simulation; render presentation has no submit API. **H5** No simulation system reads perception state. **H6** Peer identity on every command, kernel-stamped, never payload-borne; a command constructor without `issuer_peer` must not exist. **H7** Everything crossing the kernel boundary is plain data. **H8** No networking code in MVP: the only ingress is local input, the only egress local presentation. **H9** Simulation never reads wall-clock or global RNG. **H10** Kernel logic is scene-tree independent — runs headless, testable without a scene; a `Kernel.step()` call advances the sim synchronously in tests. Autoload vs node → ADR; if an autoload exists it is a thin holder of an instance that code receives as a parameter, so tests never share global state.
142	
143	**CR-15. Control plane** (host-local, not commands): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; CR-18)*, `request_shutdown`. Callers: Save/Load, the pause/Chart Table UI (host-local call), boot code. **Timing** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a request is recorded when made — from any phase, from a hook, from a P5 handler, or from outside a tick (a UI call between frames) — and served at the **next boundary**, where a boundary is the P6 of a tick or the driver's per-frame boundary service (run before any tick of the frame and, while `PAUSED`, every frame), whichever comes first; the call itself never changes state. `request_shutdown` is accepted from **every state except `SHUTTING_DOWN`** (including `BOOTING`, `LOADING` and `SAVING`; in those it is served at the boundary that follows the atomic step). Requests reaching the same boundary are applied in arrival order, never coalesced: a `request_pause` then a `request_resume` on one boundary leaves the kernel `RUNNING` with no paused service cycle run; a caller that needs a definite state re-issues the state it wants (Chart Table CT-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from chart-table-web-map-and-menus (ASK-CT-9))*. **`request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash = none)`** (K-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1; amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14: `restore_epoch` is supplied by Save/Load, whose epoch staging step has completed before the call is made: `EPOCH_DURABLE`, or a logged `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` with `save_status = FAILED`, or no advance was due. Save/Load advances the value on every death-stub restore, every `FAULT_RECOVERY` and every Continue except one of the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation, which carries it unchanged and writes nothing (R13). The kernel never waits on that write: no Save/Load I/O completes inside `LOADING`, which stays atomic within one boundary service (States). **Listed exposure (failure path, R14):** after `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` the installed epoch exists only in Save/Load's memory, so a process kill before Save/Load's next successful epoch write may replay that epoch once; G3/G4 are unaffected because they are defined given the `(save bytes, restore_epoch)` pair. The kernel holds it read-only for the session, exposes it in the `kernel.clock` read view (CR-8) and rejects a value outside the u32 range in its pre-check, `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE`)*: when an expected hash is given, the kernel recomputes `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` (D.12) after the last `post_restore()`, inside `LOADING` and before the first `RUNNING` tick, and reports `{T, computed_hash, match}` to the requester; Save/Load derives its EXACT / REBASED / mismatch verdict from it (SL-12). A mismatch is **not** a `FAULTED` transition — release plays on; policy is the requester's. Save/Load does not use restore-into-`PAUSED` for this window *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (K-4))*. **Control-plane read access:** a control-plane caller is not one of the CR-10 subscriber classes; Save/Load (the one such caller at MVP) may read `kernel.clock`, the Controller's per-seat `loco_state`, the Graph's `read_view.failures()` and an optional Attention `SIM` read view, and receives end-of-tick notifications, all read in the tick boundary in which it issues a request; it never reads `PERCEPTION_OUT`, never submits commands and never holds a `WriteScope` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-13))*. In VS-B a guest's pause or save *request* is a command defined by Session or Save/Load, validated on the host, which then calls the control API.
144	
145	**CR-16. Pause semantics.** `PAUSED` stops the tick but not rendering. While paused, submit accepts only types flagged `allowed_when_paused` by their owner, and **only non-diegetic actions may carry the flag** (save, settings, resume, menu navigation) — no gameplay verb that changes `SIM` state is allowed while paused, so a solo player cannot equip, repair or re-route with time stopped mid-tell (Dread Before Chaos), and solo pause behaves like co-op's overlay-only pause; a paused-allowed command may write only blocks registered `gameplay = false` **and** named in the type's `writes_blocks` (boot-checked, CR-6; the `WriteScope` issued in the paused cycle carries exactly that set, and a write outside it is refused and counted as `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`), never a `SIM` gameplay block *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; everything else is rejected `PAUSED` immediately, never queued, so there is no burst on resume. Admitted paused-allowed commands are dispatched by a **paused service cycle** that runs P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 with no P3 and with `T` unchanged, **once per rendered frame while `PAUSED`** (the paused boundary, which also serves control-plane requests), so a save or a menu action takes effect without advancing simulated time. At MVP no command type sets the flag; the cycle is a retained seam that only test fixtures exercise (CR-2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Commands already queued when the pause is honoured are neither dispatched by the service cycle nor rejected: they wait, in order, for the first `RUNNING` tick after resume. **Pause is single-player only**: in co-op a menu cannot stop a shared sim — VS-B treats pause as a UI overlay with the kernel `RUNNING`. The Chart Table GDD must not assume "pick a target" happens while paused. Relationship to the scene tree's pause → ADR.
146	
147	**CR-17. Bounds and overload behaviour.** At most `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` processed per tick, the rest waiting FIFO. `QUEUE_CAPACITY` total and `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY` per issuer; beyond that `QUEUE_FULL` at admission — never silent drop, never unbounded growth. Catch-up runs at most `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` ticks per frame, then lets simulated time lag rather than spiral (lag above `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` is dropped at the end of the frame, D.5); a lag counter is exposed to diagnostics. P3 exceeding `STEP_BUDGET_MS` logs the slowest hooks but the tick completes. A command older than its type's `max_age_ticks` is rejected `STALE`, so a hitch cannot unleash a second of stale intents. At the defaults `STALE` is unreachable from local ingress (the queue can hold a command at most 8 ticks and `T` does not advance while paused or saving); it is a VS-B seam for remote-stamped ticks, guarded locally by a "never stale" invariant test (Section E; ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling, R-3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
148	
149	**CR-18. Snapshot semantics.** A snapshot is taken only at a tick boundary (P6), covers all `persist` blocks at the same T, and records `(T, per-block schema_version)`. Capture is synchronous and in memory with the tick halted (`SAVING`), and **atomic within a single boundary service — `SAVING` never spans a frame**; file I/O is Save/Load's and off the critical path → ADR. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Restore replaces all `WORLD`-scoped persisted blocks atomically and leaves `PROFILE`-scoped blocks untouched (Pillar 5: losing the ship or a body never loses knowledge); partial restore within a scope is unsupported; failure aborts to `FAULTED` with pre-restore state intact where possible. With join-in-progress deferred, the same snapshot/restore contract is VS-B's guest transfer at session start, so it must be complete and cheap. **New game (K-2):** a new game passes through `LOADING`: every block takes `default_state()`, Save/Load's `new_game(world_seed)` sets `world_seed` into `kernel.clock` *(a new game is entered by the control-plane call `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch = 0)`, valid from `BOOTING` (the first boot, States table), `RUNNING`, `PAUSED` and `FAULTED` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, so a second new game in one process — for example "death = restart from the last autosave" when no autosave exists yet — has a path; it flushes the queue with `Dropped(RELOAD)` exactly like `request_restore`, resets `T` to 0, installs the supplied epoch (a fresh slot's `slot_epoch.bin` starts at 0, Save/Load SL-18, SL-23; amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14) and leaves `PROFILE`-scoped blocks untouched: Pillar 5, a new world never loses knowledge; what a new crew keeps is Open Question 13, Save/Load's) (Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, then each owner that registered an `init_world(world_seed)` step runs it in `restore_after` order under one `WriteScope`, before `post_restore()`; at MVP the world build is Web Map & Transit's `init_world` (WM-7), which calls the Layout, Graph and Body mutators in its fixed order *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-18) and web-map-and-transit)*. The last step of every pass through `LOADING`, restore or new game, is the CR-7 binding rebuild (after the `init_world` steps and `post_restore()`, and after a restore's K-4 hash check), so the first `RUNNING` tick already sees the rebuilt `PlayerId → {(block_id, entity_id)}` half *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
150	
151	**CR-19. Fault channel, violations and build profiles** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; replaces the earlier 'throws / asserts' model)*. GDScript has no `try`/`catch`: a runtime script error is printed by the engine, aborts the function it occurred in and hands control back to the caller with a default value the caller cannot distinguish from a result; and `assert()` is compiled out of release exports. The kernel therefore **never relies on an exception or an assertion for control flow**, and every behaviour in this document is identical in debug and release unless a clause calls it a `STRICT_DEBUG` extra.
152	- **(a) Fault channel and the one callable contract** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R3; defines the contract once)*. **Kernel-invoked owner callables** are a closed list: `validate`, `apply`, step hooks, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state`, `read_view`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline`, `init_world`, and the result- and subscriber-handlers. The kernel calls each through `Callable.call()` and passes a context object as the last argument (`ApplyContext`/`WriteScope`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`, `NotifyContext`). **Results flow through `ctx`, never through the return value**: `validate(cmd, views, ctx)` reports through `ctx.ok()` or `ctx.reject(reason)`; `snapshot(ctx)`, `default_state(ctx)` and `read_view(ctx)` deliver their payload through `ctx.put(payload)`; `apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx)`, hooks, `restore`, `post_restore`, `init_world`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` and handlers report only success-by-completion; every callable reports failure with `ctx.fault(code, detail)`. **Every callable's only return statement is `return ctx.complete()`** (a typed token, (b)); no owner callable is declared `-> void`, because a `void` GDScript function cannot return the token and the engine's default for an aborted typed function would alias a legitimate result. A `validate` that calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()` is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`; the first outcome call stands and a second is a violation (`CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`). **Published mutators are not on this list**: other owners, not the kernel, call them, so the kernel cannot check their sentinel; they take the shared `WriteScope`, report with `scope.fault(code, detail)` and return a status that callers propagate — which is also why the sentinel's blind spot (below) is closed by status propagation. The kernel checks `ctx.faulted` (which includes any fault a mutator reported on the shared scope) and the completion token after **every** kernel-invoked call, before using its result. A fault in `apply`, a hook, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `init_world`, `default_state`, `commit_baseline` or `snap_baseline` (and in a mutator they called) moves the kernel to `FAULTED`; **a fault in `read_view` never does**: views are obtained by presentation at render time, outside any tick, and a HUD read must not be able to halt the ship (CR-11, H4) — it is recorded and counted (`INCOMPLETE` or the violation, as a P5 handler's is), the reader receives an empty view, and when sim code called it inside P2/P3 the enclosing `apply` or hook fails through the status it propagates; a fault reported by `validate` does not reject, it faults (a defect), whereas `ctx.reject(reason)` is the ordinary domain rejection (`Rejected(VALIDATION_FAILED(reason))`, kernel stays `RUNNING`); a fault in a P5 or result handler is recorded and counted but cannot fault the kernel (the tick is committed).
153	- **(b) Completion sentinel.** The kernel arms `ctx.completed = false` and a fresh `ctx.token` before each call; `ctx.complete()` sets `completed` and returns that token — a typed, non-nil, non-zero object (a per-call `CompletionToken` instance) that the kernel compares **by identity**, so a `null`, `0`, `false` or empty value returned by an aborted or forgetful function can never read as success. A call that returns anything but the armed token with `completed` set (the script aborted on an engine error, or forgot) is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` for `apply`, hooks, `validate`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` and `init_world`, and a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic, without a fault, for a P5 or result handler and for `read_view` (which returns an empty view). In a release build the sentinel is the only abort guard (`assert` is compiled out), so it is exercised on a release export in the spike (Acceptance Criteria, KRN-CTX-06). The sentinel catches a *function that aborted*; it cannot catch an error in a nested helper that the outer function then ignores — which is why mutators also return statuses and callers must propagate them.
154	- **(c) What cannot be done.** Engine script errors cannot be intercepted. P5 subscriber isolation is therefore **best-effort plus lint**: the kernel calls handlers one at a time from its own loop, so an aborted handler does not stop the loop; the sentinel names the offending subscriber in diagnostics; a lint forbids handlers from calling anything that can write.
155	- **(d) Violations.** A *violation* (write outside a `WriteScope`, a sim read of `PERCEPTION_OUT`, a hook reaching the `PLAYER` ingress, a submit during `SAVING`, a payload that passed the size check but fails the round-trip, a `SIM` hash change at the tripwire) is, in every build: the offending action refused, a named diagnostics counter incremented, `push_error` called. Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the kernel additionally calls the injected `violation_handler(code, detail)`; the dev default halts via `assert(false)`, the test default records. No state-machine outcome (`FAULTED`, reject reasons, results) differs between profiles.
156	- **(e) KernelProfile.** `KernelProfile` ∈ {`STRICT_DEBUG`, `LENIENT_RELEASE`} is injected at construction (H10) and never read from `OS.is_debug_build()` inside the kernel, so one test process can construct a kernel per profile and exercise both branches. `STRICT_DEBUG` enables only the extras: the per-command serialization round-trip (CR-4), the violation handler, the `SIM` tripwire (CR-12) and the counter test seams.
157	
158	**Velocity rule (gameplay-programmer, adopted as an acceptance criterion).** Adding a new command verb touches at most two files: one handler and one registration line. If the kernel ever makes a feature cost more than that, the layer will be bypassed — which is the exact lapse TD-FEASIBILITY named. Hence: commands are plain data records (no class per verb), state blocks are coarse (one per domain system, not per entity), and replay/undo/rollback/middleware are deferred.
159	
160	### States and Transitions
