content.content:
51	### Core Rules
52	
53	*Specialists consulted: systems-designer (primary), gameplay-programmer (feel/feasibility), engine-programmer (Godot 4.7.2 integration). Their one disagreement — tick rate — is resolved in CR-1. Items tagged **→ ADR** are engine-integration choices deliberately left out of this behaviour spec.*
54	
55	**Vocabulary.** *Tick*: one fixed-step iteration of the authoritative simulation; tick number `T` is a monotonically increasing integer and the only clock the simulation knows. *State block*: a named, versioned, single-owner container of domain state registered with the kernel. *Command*: a serializable request to change state, carrying issuer identity. *Owner*: the domain system that is the only writer of a block. *Read view*: the read-only accessor an owner publishes. *Step hook*: owner-registered code that runs in the propagation phase. *Mode*: `HOST` (authoritative; the only mode in MVP) or `MIRROR` (VS-B guest: receives state, runs no authoritative tick) — the public API is identical in both. *PlayerId*: a stable seat identity (1 in single-player; PlayerId 0 is reserved as "no seat" — additive, provisional *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics)*); *peer_id*: the transport identity of a connection (host = 1). Persistent per-player state is keyed by PlayerId, never by peer_id, because peer IDs are reassigned per connection (this corrects the systems index's "keyed by peer ID" for Sanity and Suit).
56	
57	**CR-1. Fixed tick at `TICK_RATE` = 60 Hz, with per-hook step divisors.** The simulation advances in steps of exactly `1/TICK_RATE` seconds of *simulated* time, independent of render frame time; durations everywhere are in ticks (the Attention tell window of 10–30 s is 600–1800 ticks). The kernel never reads wall-clock time or `delta`. Input- and physics-adjacent hooks run every tick; slow systems run at a divisor (Graph 6 → 10 Hz, Attention 6, Suit vitals 6, Sanity drift 12 → 5 Hz).
58	*Rationale and alternatives.* The gameplay-programmer argued for a 20 Hz kernel (slow systems don't need more; worst-case 50 ms latency is invisible behind immediate local acknowledgement) but set a hard floor of 15 Hz and would push back at 10. The engine-programmer argued for tick = physics rate so the moving ship body and the characters inside it share one timeline (*historical*: CR-1a later settled that the tick is driven from `_process`, not the physics step, and Body integrates ship-local kinematics inside the sim, so physics alignment is no longer a reason for any `TICK_RATE`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. 60 Hz + divisors satisfies both: one clock, submit-to-applied within one tick (16.7 ms of simulated time) on an empty queue, and the cost profile of a 10 Hz graph. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A variable timestep was rejected (breaks replay, tests and save equivalence); a 30 Hz kernel sits at a 2:1 ratio to the 60 fps render rate (alternate frames run 0 and 1 ticks), not at an awkward one to the physics step, which is not the clock. The tick *source* is settled in CR-1a (a `TickDriver` with an injected delta, not the physics callback); `step()` stays a plain method that tests and a future server call directly. Changing `TICK_RATE` later invalidates every tuned value expressed in ticks. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
59	
60	**CR-1a. Tick driver, clock source and catch-up** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; closes former Open Question 2, the technical-director confirms it in the spike)*. `Kernel.step()` has no clock. A `TickDriver` (a `RefCounted`, no scene tree) owns the accumulator, receives time as an injected integer count of microseconds (`delta_us`), and is driven by exactly one node with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` from its `_process(delta)`; that node converts the engine's `delta` to `delta_us` once, and that conversion plus the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads in the project (H9). **Godot's physics step is not the clock**: at MVP the avatar has no physics body (CR-13), so nothing needs the physics callback, and the driver needs no coupling to `physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame` (the former coupled constraint 4 is deleted). A later Vertical Slice physics projection runs in `_physics_process` as a `PROJECTOR` reading committed state and never steps the kernel. The accumulator is an integer in units of *microseconds × TICK_RATE*, so one tick is exactly `TICK_UNITS` = 1,000,000 units for every integer `TICK_RATE` (no float drift, no boundary flips); each frame that begins (after the boundary service) with the kernel `RUNNING` adds `acc += delta_us × TICK_RATE`. **Order of the add against the clear** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the boundary service runs first; if it moved the kernel into `RUNNING` (a resume, a load, a finished save) the accumulator is cleared and **that frame's own `delta_us` is discarded** — the frame runs 0 ticks, because its wall time was spent paused, loading or saving — and the add applies from the next frame on; a frame that finds the kernel not `RUNNING` adds nothing. Per frame the driver (1) runs the boundary service (CR-15) before any tick; (2) while the kernel is `RUNNING`, runs `step()` `ticks_run = min(floor(acc / TICK_UNITS), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)` times, **re-reading the kernel state after every `step()`** and stopping (and clearing `acc`) the moment it is no longer `RUNNING` — a P6 pause, a restore, a fault; (3) applies lag forgiveness (D.5); (4) flushes the result buffer (CR-5); (5) while `PAUSED`, runs the paused boundary service (CR-16). **The accumulator is cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`** (from `LOADING`, `PAUSED` or `SAVING`), so a load, an autosave or a pause never produces catch-up ticks afterwards. The driver node has a process priority that runs it before the presentation nodes, so presentation reads the tick the driver just produced. **Step 0 — input sample, and the priority table** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: nothing in the driver's step list sampled input, so the best-case latency of D.4 rested on an unstated ordering. The order inside one rendered frame is now fixed by process priority (lower runs first): **(0)** the input adapter (an `INPUT_SURFACE` object; it reads the engine's input state for this frame and calls `submit`, so its commands are admitted before the boundary service and the tick loop); **(1)** the `TickDriver` node (boundary service, then the tick loop, then forgiveness, result flush, paused service); **(2)** presentation nodes (Pixel-Perfect pipeline, HUD, Lighting, Audio), which read what the driver just committed. The adapter's priority is therefore strictly below the driver's number; a presentation node must sort after the driver (a lint on `process_priority` values; the engine reference is silent on ordering between nodes, so the spike verifies it, KRN-LAT-02). Tests call `Kernel.step()` directly, or inject `delta_us` into the driver; nothing in the kernel sleeps or reads a clock. **Main thread and `Engine.time_scale`**: the kernel, the driver and every owner callable run on the main thread only — no worker thread calls `submit`, a read view or a mutator (a lint forbids `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` and `call_deferred` into kernel code); `_process(delta)`'s `delta` is scaled by `Engine.time_scale` in the engine's contract as we read it (the pinned engine reference does not state it — **[UNV]**, verify in the spike), so release builds pin `Engine.time_scale = 1.0` (a boot check records `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT` in diagnostics otherwise) and a dev build that changes it knowingly scales simulated speed through `delta` — ticks stay exact integers either way.

62	**CR-2. Tick phase order.** Each tick executes these phases to completion, in order, with no interleaving:
63	
64	| # | Phase | What happens | Who may write blocks |
65	|---|-------|--------------|----------------------|
66	| P0 | Begin | Tick counter increments; the pending set is *frozen* as this tick's candidate set (commands arriving now wait for T+1) | nobody |
67	| P1 | Intake | Candidate set in ordering-key order (CR-13) — a sort only when a non-monotone (remote) insert happened since the last tick, otherwise the head of an already-ordered queue — the first `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` form this tick's **batch**; the overflow returns to the unfrozen pending set in order and stays supersedable (Section E) | nobody |
68	| P2 | Dispatch | Per command in order: authority check → validate → apply or reject (CR-5) | the handler, inside `apply` only |
69	| P3 | Step | Step hooks in resolved order (CR-3); a hook runs when `T mod divisor == offset` | the hook's own block, plus owner-published mutators of other blocks (CR-9) |
70	| P4 | Commit | Dirty sets finalised; "tick committed" marker advances; interpolation baseline captured (`commit_baseline()` on each `interpolated` block — a kernel-run roll of a **derived presentation cache**, not a block write: the baseline is excluded from `snapshot()`, `canonical_bytes` and every hash, and is rebuilt by `snap_baseline` on every transition into `RUNNING`, so it has no canonical status and "nobody writes" stays true) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | nobody |
71	| P5 | Notify | Batched change notifications delivered (CR-10), then the result buffer is flushed (CR-5) | nobody — writes disabled |
72	| P6 | Boundary services | Pending control-plane requests in arrival order (CR-15), pending snapshot (Saving), command-log append | the kernel only |

74	P2 commands see earlier P2 effects in the same tick; P3 sees all of P2; subscribers and presentation only ever see post-P4 state, never a half-applied tick. **Paused service cycle** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; a retained seam that only test fixtures exercise at MVP, because no MVP command type sets `allowed_when_paused`)*: on every rendered frame while `PAUSED` the driver runs the paused boundary service — P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 with no P0 and no P3, `T` unchanged — dispatching only commands of `allowed_when_paused` types (CR-16). It is a deliberate carve-out from the running-tick guarantees: its commits apply at the current `T` (`apply_tick == queued_tick` is legal there, unlike a running tick), several commits can share one `T`, and G1/G2/G3 hold for it only as CR-13 states.

76	**CR-3. Step hooks and ordering.** Hooks register `(hook_id, owner, divisor, offset, after: [hook_id | {hook_id, tolerates_stale}])`. The kernel resolves a total order by topological sort of `after`; ties break by registration order, then `hook_id`. A cycle or unknown `hook_id` fails boot (CR-6). Sim-to-sim data flow within a tick is "reader declares `after` writer" (Suit vitals `after: graph.propagate.atmo` — the Graph registers three chained hooks, see its LS-1 *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check, routed from the Life-Support Graph GDD)*). The order is data: testable, and printable by the Debug Overlay. An `after` edge between two hooks that never run in the same tick (Section E) must carry `tolerates_stale: true` if the reader accepts data up to a divisor old; boot warns only for **undeclared** mismatches, so the real boot (`horror.step` divisor 5 after `attention.step` divisor 6, the Graph's staggered chain — `.atmo` (6, 2) after `.power` (6, 0), `.failure` (6, 4) after `.atmo` — and the other cross-offset pairs of Section E) stays silent once declared and the warning keeps its meaning *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Hooks may not submit `PLAYER`-origin commands; they may submit `SYSTEM`-origin ones (CR-4) through `submit_system(type, payload, dedupe_key = none)` and may ask `has_pending(type, dedupe_key)` (CR-9 owner rule).

78	**CR-4. Command anatomy, origin and intents.** A command is plain serializable data:
79	
80	| Field | Meaning |
81	|-------|---------|
82	| `type` | Registered command type ID, owned by a domain system |
83	| `issuer_peer` | Stamped by the kernel's ingress — never taken from the payload |
84	| `origin` | `PLAYER` or `SYSTEM`, stamped by ingress |
85	| `actor` | The entity the command acts as: an opaque ID in the ID space of the type's declared `actor_source` block (CR-7; IDs are block-local, CR-8, so one number can name different entities in two blocks), or none *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
86	| `seq` | Monotonically increasing integer per `(issuer_peer, origin)` — the host's `PLAYER` and `SYSTEM` streams are separate spaces *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Stamped by the kernel at ISSUED, never chosen by a local caller**: every local `INPUT_SURFACE` handle and `submit_system()` receives the next value of the one kernel-held counter for its `(issuer_peer, origin)`, so any number of surfaces sharing the `(1, PLAYER)` space can never collide; the counter advances on every submit, including one rejected at admission, so locally stamped values are dense (1, 2, 3 …) and `DUPLICATE_SEQ` and gap counting apply only to a `seq` supplied by the **test ingress or a remote ingress** (the only two callers that may supply one) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)* |
87	| `correlation` | Optional opaque `int` the submitting caller attaches (default 0 = none); the kernel never interprets it and echoes it unchanged in the command's result record and in any rejection event, so a caller (the Player Controller's pre-play tokens, a menu) matches a result to the act that caused it without learning or choosing `seq`. Kernel metadata like `submission_id`, never payload-borne; not part of `canonical_bytes` or any hash. Not unique: two submits may carry the same `correlation` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)* |
88	| `payload` | Plain data only, per the recursive whitelist below; no object references, node paths or callables; `var_to_bytes(payload, false).size()` ≤ `MAX_PAYLOAD` |
89	| `queued_tick` | Stamped on enqueue |
90	| `submission_id` | Kernel metadata, never payload-borne: a kernel-unique counter stamped at ISSUED, before admission, so even a rejected submit has one; it is the `result_id` of the command's result (CR-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

92	*Discrete commands vs continuous intents.* If the sim must log, validate, save or replay it, it is a command (examples; each type's owner GDD is authoritative: Controller `set_move_intent`, `set_aim`, `toggle_beam`; Interaction `begin_cut` (module salvage, V8), `begin_patch`, `cancel_channel`, `pickup`, `drop`, `set_switch`, `field_check`; Modular Ship Assembly `begin_weld` (declared by Interaction, registered by Assembly), `begin_seam_cut`, `install_module` and the `SYSTEM`-only completions `weld` / `seam_cut` (registry: `assembly_commands`; there is no `remove_module` — it is reserved and unregistered, and V8 salvage is the only removal); Suit `equip_tool` (its only type); Web Map & Transit `pod_hop`, `berth`, `unberth` and the `SYSTEM`-only `pod_arrive`, `pod_settle`, `berth_step`, `web_reconcile` (registry: `web_commands`). `interact` is an input action, not a command type, and `use_item` has no owner and is not a command *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system, suit-and-equipment, modular-ship-assembly and web-map-and-transit)*). What the stick is doing *right now* is an intent: intents are commands too, but a type may declare `coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK` — coalescing happens at admission over the unfrozen queue, keyed `(type, actor, issuer_peer)`, the older command becoming `Superseded` — and the input adapter sends one only when the quantised value changes — a few per second, never one per tick. Edge-triggered inputs (press, release, confirm) must declare `coalesce = NONE` or taps are lost. Movement integration runs inside the sim: Body's `body.integrate` hook (divisor 1, P3) reads the current intent and integrates ship-local kinematics (CR-13), so a move intent takes effect one tick after it is submitted, like every command; there is no physics-side integration at MVP, and position ownership is settled (Body owns it; the Controller owns intent and facing) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Under `STRICT_DEBUG` every command is round-tripped through serialization before dispatch, even locally; one that cannot survive is a violation (CR-19). **Submit is fire-and-forget and never calls back**: `submit()` returns nothing and invokes no callback, handler or subscriber, so it is safe to call from any handler, hook or result handler; its only outcome is one result record appended to the kernel's result buffer (CR-5), delivered at the next flush and identified by `result_id` — a remote issuer could never get a synchronous answer, so the local one doesn't either *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `submit()` takes the optional `correlation` and returns nothing, not even a receipt: the caller learns the outcome only from the result record, which carries its `correlation` back, so "fire-and-forget" is literally true and `seq` stays the kernel's. The API shape is `submit(type, payload, actor = none, correlation = 0)` on an `INPUT_SURFACE` handle and `submit_system(type, payload, dedupe_key = none)` for hooks (a hook needs no correlation: it never receives a result) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*.
93	
94	**Payload whitelist** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. 'Plain' is a recursive `Variant.Type` whitelist checked at admission: `NIL`, `BOOL`, `INT`, `FLOAT` (finite only — `NaN` and `±inf` are `MALFORMED`; the same finite check applies to **each component of a `VECTOR2` and each element of `PackedFloat32Array`, `PackedFloat64Array` and `PackedVector2Array`**, which the walk visits in O(n) bounded by `MAX_PAYLOAD` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), `STRING`, `STRING_NAME`, `VECTOR2`, `VECTOR2I`, the `Packed{Byte,Int32,Int64,Float32,Float64,String,Vector2}Array` types, and `ARRAY`/`DICTIONARY` of the same, to a depth cap `PAYLOAD_MAX_DEPTH` = 8 (which also rejects a self-containing container). Dictionary keys must be `INT`, `STRING` or `STRING_NAME` and **all keys of one dictionary must share one type** (mixed keys have no canonical order, D.12). Anything else — an `Object`, `NodePath`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, a non-whitelisted `Variant.Type`, a non-finite float, a depth-9 nesting, mixed dictionary keys — is `MALFORMED`; the size bound is measured as `var_to_bytes(payload, false).size()` after the walk passes. Immediate *acknowledgement* (a tool sound, a hand animation, a linear progress bar starting) is presentation's job and happens in the same frame; the sim confirms on the next tick. The latency bounds are stated once, in Game Feel and D.4.
95	
96	**CR-5. Command lifecycle and the exactly-one-result guarantee.** Every command reaches exactly one terminal state and emits exactly one result record (identified by `result_id`; delivered to its issuer unless it is `SYSTEM`-origin, see Result identity and delivery below). Stages: *Issued* → *Admission* (kernel state accepts commands; type registered; **origin allowed for the type — known at admission, so rejected there**; queue not full; `seq` not a duplicate — gaps are accepted and counted, not rejected; issuer rate limit; payload plain) → *Queued* → *Authority check* in P2 (origin re-checked as a defence in depth; if the type declares `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, the binding table says the issuer controls the key `(actor_source, actor)` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; age ≤ the type's `max_age_ticks`) → *Validate* (owner's side-effect-free `validate(cmd, views, ctx)`: it reports through `ctx.ok()` or `ctx.reject(reason)` — a domain reason — and ends with `return ctx.complete()`; its return value carries no outcome, CR-19(a)/(b)) → *Apply* (`apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx)`, ending with `return ctx.complete()`; infallible by contract once validate passed, CR-9) → terminal: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R3)*
97	
98	| Terminal | Meaning |
99	|----------|---------|
100	| `Applied` | Effects are in state as of tick T (a command dispatched earlier in a tick that then faults is still `Applied`, with `detail.uncommitted = 1`) |
101	| `Rejected(reason)` | No effect |
102	| `Dropped(reason)` | Never evaluated: a reload, a shutdown or a fault flushed it — `RELOAD`, `SHUTDOWN`, `FAULTED` (the last added so G5 holds on the defect path). Includes the not-yet-dispatched commands of a faulting tick's batch *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
103	| `Faulted(code)` | Evaluated, and its `validate` or `apply` (or a mutator it called) reported a fault through the fault channel (CR-19): effects may be partial and are unreachable to presentation. Exactly one command per fault — the cause. Distinct from `Rejected` (not 'no effect') and `Dropped` (not 'never evaluated') *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
104	| `Superseded` | Coalesced away by a newer command of a coalescing type |
105	
106	Kernel reject reasons are a closed set: `NOT_ACCEPTING`, `PAUSED`, `UNKNOWN_TYPE`, `QUEUE_FULL`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `DUPLICATE_SEQ`, `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, `STALE`, `MALFORMED`, `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)` — domain codes are namespaced and owned by the registering system (Interaction's set, e.g. `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `PRECONDITION`, `BUSY`, is its GDD's). The result record carries `result_id`, `issuer_peer`, `origin`, `seq`, `correlation`, `ok`, `reason`, `subject` (the target the rejection refers to), an optional `detail` dictionary of numbers, and `tick` — **never display strings** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `result_id` and `origin` added)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2: `correlation` added, echoed unchanged from the submit)*. Presentation maps reasons to sound, shake or tooltip. **Reason codes are computed from true state and the kernel never filters them.** That is the whole of the kernel's claim. Whether, when and how cheaply a reason reaches the player is *not* the kernel's: Interaction, Sanity and the HUD own it and must obey Pillar 4's cost rule (a check costs time, risk or trust) — for example surfacing a `PRECONDITION` only after channel time has been spent, or only through diegetic feedback rather than an instant tooltip. *Design test (CD-GDD-ALIGN):* if a rejection lets the player falsify a hallucination at zero time, risk or trust cost, the presentation of that rejection is wrong — not the kernel. A command *aborted mid-channel* (power drops during a cut) is reported by the channel owner through state change, not through the command result. The kernel never retries.
107	
108	**Result identity and delivery** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A result is identified by `result_id` (the command's `submission_id`). A local issuer correlates by the `correlation` it attached to the submit (echoed unchanged; the caller's own uniqueness, not the kernel's), never by `seq`, which a local caller neither chooses nor learns *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*. `(issuer_peer, origin, seq)` is unique among results **except** `DUPLICATE_SEQ` rejections, which by definition repeat an earlier command's `(issuer_peer, origin, seq)` and are told apart by `result_id` and `reason`; only a test or remote ingress can produce one (see the `seq` row of CR-4). Every terminal result — admission rejections, `Superseded`, P2 results, `Dropped(...)`, `Faulted` — is appended to the kernel's **result buffer** in the order it occurs; `submit()` itself never delivers. The buffer is flushed (a) at P5 of every tick, after the change batch, and (b) by the driver once per rendered frame after that frame's ticks, **in every kernel state** (`BOOTING`, `LOADING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`, and an idle frame with no tick), so `NOT_ACCEPTING`, `PAUSED`, `Dropped(RELOAD|SHUTDOWN|FAULTED)` and every other result always have a delivery point. A flush swaps the buffer out before delivering: whatever a result handler submits (the STALE resubmit of Section E, for example) is admitted normally, and any result it produces lands in the fresh buffer and is delivered at the next flush, never recursively — a handler that resubmits on every rejection costs one result per flush and cannot loop. Results go to the issuing `INPUT_SURFACE`'s result handler and to the diagnostics log. **`SYSTEM`-origin results are never delivered to a subscriber or to the submitting owner** (owners never subscribe, CR-10); they go to the command log and the diagnostics counters only, and an owner that needs the outcome reads state. **Fault semantics (a designer decision, not an implementer detail)**: when the kernel faults, each command already dispatched in the faulting tick whose `apply` completed receives `Applied` with `detail.uncommitted = 1` (its effects are in the live blocks although P4 never ran); the faulting command receives `Faulted(code)`; every not-yet-dispatched batch command and every pending command receives `Dropped(FAULTED)`; all are buffered at the fault transition and delivered at the next frame flush.
109	
110	**CR-6. Registration at boot, then frozen.** Block, command-type, hook, diagnostics-channel and binding-source registration are legal only in `BOOTING` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from debug-overlay-true-values (E-DO-38))* (a block may declare one optional `binding_source` callable, CR-7; one registered after `BOOTING` is refused like every other registration *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*); after `BOOTING → LOADING` the registries are immutable until shutdown. Registration is an explicit declaration by the composition root, not discovery via the scene tree. Duplicate IDs, unknown types, missing owners and hook cycles fail boot loudly in every build. A command type registered without `allowed_origins`, `actor_binding`, `coalesce` or `max_age_ticks` (**no silent defaults**: an omitted `actor_binding` must never mean 'no ownership check'), a type with `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER` but no `actor_source`, one whose `actor_source` names a block that registered no `binding_source`, and a `NONE` type that declares an `actor_source` (each fails boot with `ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID`, naming the type) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, a block registered without `class`, `gameplay`, `repl_hint` or `persist`, a type whose `writes_blocks` names an unregistered block, and an `allowed_when_paused` type whose `writes_blocks` names any `gameplay = true` block likewise fail boot (`BOOTING → FAULTED`) naming the registration. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A type with `coalesce ≠ NONE` that allows both origins fails boot (`COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN`), because the supersession key carries no origin (D.8); and the joint memory assertion of Section G constraint 8 is checked here *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
111	
112	**CR-7. Authority model (behaviour).** The host is the sole authority: only a `HOST` kernel ticks and applies; a `MIRROR` never applies. Each command type's owner declares `allowed_origins ⊆ {PLAYER, SYSTEM}` and `actor_binding ∈ {NONE, OWNED_BY_ISSUER}` — both mandatory (CR-6) — and `allowed_origins` is checked at admission, with a P2 re-check as defence in depth. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A type with `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER` also declares **`actor_source`**: the `block_id` of the registered binding source whose ID space its `actor` belongs to (`body.state` for every avatar-acting type, `emitter.state` for `toggle_beam`). The P2 authority check passes iff `(actor_source(type), actor) ∈ half_b[PlayerId(issuer_peer)]`. So an actor and a beam with the same number can never stand in for each other. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* `SYSTEM` commands never arrive from a network; remote ingress always stamps `PLAYER`. The kernel holds a **binding table** — `peer_id → PlayerId` and `PlayerId → {(source block_id, entity_id)}` — as identity data, not domain state; the table has two halves with different lifetimes *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6 (user delegated all remaining calls): the kernel owns the rebuild; closes Body Open Question 30)*. **(a) `peer_id → PlayerId`** is session state: it is mutated only through a host-only API called by the session owner (a boot step in MVP: `HOST_PEER_ID` 1 → PlayerId 1; Co-op Session in VS-B), and a restore, a death restart or a new game never touches it and never resets any issuer's `seq` or `last_seq`. **(b) `PlayerId → {(source block_id, entity_id)}`** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* is derived from saved state and is never saved: **the kernel rebuilds it itself as the last step of every pass through `LOADING`** (`request_restore` and `request_new_game` alike), after the last `post_restore()` and the K-4 hash check and before the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition. The rebuild clears half (b) entirely, then calls each registered **binding source** (CR-6, CR-8) in ascending `block_id` order — with `ctx`, as a pure read of its owner's block, under no `WriteScope`, ending `return ctx.complete()` — which delivers `[(player_id, entity_id)]` in ascending order through `ctx.put`, and binds every pair under the source's own `block_id`: each delivered `(player_id, entity_id)` is stored as `player_id → (source_block_id, entity_id)`. Entity IDs are block-local (CR-8: each owner allocates from its own counter and the kernel allocates none), so the key always carries the source. Equal numbers from two sources (Body actor 1 and Emitter beam 1) are two different keys and never conflict. A key `(source_block_id, entity_id)` delivered for two different PlayerIds, or the same triple `(player_id, source_block_id, entity_id)` delivered twice, is `BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT`. A source that reports `ctx.fault` or returns without the sentinel is that source's fault. Either one takes `LOADING → FAULTED` naming the source. The checks compare keys only within one source. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; registry request: `kernel_binding_table` `half_b`, `errors`, `actor_source`, `referenced_by`)* Because `LOADING` is atomic within one boundary service, the rebuild is not a P6 control-plane request and no command can interleave with it; the P6 rule (Section E) governs session-owner changes to half (a) only. At MVP no binding source's pairs change during `RUNNING`, so no `RUNNING` tick sees an empty or stale half (b); a runtime seat or beam reassignment (VS-B) is a session-owner request honoured at P6 (Open Question 4, the co-op ADR). MVP binding sources: Body's `seat_bindings()` (its `SEAT` rows → `(seat, actor_id)`) and the Emitter's `beam_bindings()` (`(player_id, beam_id)`). Single-player: PlayerId 1 → {(`body.state`, avatar actor_id), (`emitter.state`, beam_id)}. Both numbers may be 1 (two independent counters), and the result is valid. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix. Resolved 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix (G6): keyed by source rather than by namespace-tagged IDs, so Body's and the Emitter's persisted ID formats stay unchanged (G1).)* *(Alternative: Player Controller owns the binding as a block — rejected because the kernel could then not authority-check without calling a domain system. → ADR.)* **Single-player is not a special case**: local input is `PLAYER`-origin peer 1 (registry: `HOST_PEER_ID` = 1) acting on an entity peer 1 is bound to; the authority stage runs on every command from day one, so TD-FEASIBILITY's "authority discipline lapsing" risk is structural, not disciplinary. The kernel checks *who*; owners validate *whether the world allows it*; the kernel encodes no game rules. For friendly harm the kernel checks only issuer→actor ownership; the "attacker below the sanity threshold" gate is Interaction's `validate` calling Sanity's query on the actor's authoritative sanity level (a `SIM` block), never on anyone's perception.
113	
114	**CR-8. State-block registry contract.** An owner registers: `block_id` (unique, namespaced, e.g. `graph.state`); `owner`; `schema_version` (bumped on any serialized-shape change); `class` ∈ {`SIM`, `PERCEPTION_OUT`} (CR-12); `persist` (false = derived, rebuilt after load) and, when true, `persist_scope` ∈ {`WORLD`, `PROFILE`} — `WORLD` blocks live in the world snapshot and roll back on `request_restore`; `PROFILE` blocks (decoded rules, lore, scars: Pillar 5's "never knowledge") live outside it and are never rolled back by a world restore; `scope` ∈ {`SHARED`, `PER_PLAYER` keyed by PlayerId}; `gameplay` (bool, mandatory: true when a gameplay verb can change the block; false only for settings, menu and save-request state — the CR-16 paused-write test) and `interpolated` (bool, default false: when true the kernel calls the owner's `commit_baseline()` at P4 so the previous/current pair rolls exactly once per tick, and after a restore or an owner-declared teleport/reset the owner calls `snap_baseline(key)` so presentation never interpolates across a discontinuity) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `repl_hint` ∈ {`HOST_ONLY`, `SHARED_SUMMARY`, `OWNER_PRIVATE`} — mandatory now though unused until VS-B, so no block ever ships without the decision; `snapshot(ctx)` (delivers its plain data through `ctx.put(payload)` and ends with `return ctx.complete()`; canonical state only, deterministic ordering, entity references by stable ID, no derived caches; **the payload is a deep copy** — `duplicate_deep()` for Dictionary/Array, `duplicate()` for Packed arrays, which GDScript passes by reference — never a reference into live state); `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` (whole-block replace; **copies in** and never retains a reference to `data`, so two restores from one payload cannot alias; the owner migrates from `stored_version`; an unsupported version is a reported failure through the fault channel, never a silent default) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `default_state(ctx)` (when a save lacks the block; `ctx.put(state)`); `post_restore(ctx)` (after *all* blocks restore: resolve cross-block IDs, rebuild caches, check invariants); `read_view(ctx)` (the kernel's view-issuing surface calls it and hands the reader `ctx.put(view)`'s content: a getter-only facade or a copy — never a live container, CR-12); The kernel therefore **never relies on an exception or an assertion for control flow**, and every behaviour in this document is identical in debug and release unless a clause calls it a `STRICT_DEBUG` extra.
152	- **(a) Fault channel and the one callable contract** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R3; defines the contract once)*. **Kernel-invoked owner callables** are a closed list: `validate`, `apply`, step hooks, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state`, `read_view`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline`, `init_world`, and the result- and subscriber-handlers. The kernel calls each through `Callable.call()` and passes a context object as the last argument (`ApplyContext`/`WriteScope`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`, `NotifyContext`). **Results flow through `ctx`, never through the return value**: `validate(cmd, views, ctx)` reports through `ctx.ok()` or `ctx.reject(reason)`; `snapshot(ctx)`, `default_state(ctx)` and `read_view(ctx)` deliver their payload through `ctx.put(payload)`; `apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx)`, hooks, `restore`, `post_restore`, `init_world`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` and handlers report only success-by-completion; every callable reports failure with `ctx.fault(code, detail)`. **Every callable's only return statement is `return ctx.complete()`** (a typed token, (b)); no owner callable is declared `-> void`, because a `void` GDScript function cannot return the token and the engine's default for an aborted typed function would alias a legitimate result. A `validate` that calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()` is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`; the first outcome call stands and a second is a violation (`CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`). **Published mutators are not on this list**: other owners, not the kernel, call them, so the kernel cannot check their sentinel; they take the shared `WriteScope`, report with `scope.fault(code, detail)` and return a status that callers propagate — which is also why the sentinel's blind spot (below) is closed by status propagation. The kernel checks `ctx.faulted` (which includes any fault a mutator reported on the shared scope) and the completion token after **every** kernel-invoked call, before using its result. A fault in `apply`, a hook, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `init_world`, `default_state`, `commit_baseline` or `snap_baseline` (and in a mutator they called) moves the kernel to `FAULTED`; **a fault in `read_view` never does**: views are obtained by presentation at render time, outside any tick, and a HUD read must not be able to halt the ship (CR-11, H4) — it is recorded and counted (`INCOMPLETE` or the violation, as a P5 handler's is), the reader receives an empty view, and when sim code called it inside P2/P3 the enclosing `apply` or hook fails through the status it propagates; a fault reported by `validate` does not reject, it faults (a defect), whereas `ctx.reject(reason)` is the ordinary domain rejection (`Rejected(VALIDATION_FAILED(reason))`, kernel stays `RUNNING`); a fault in a P5 or result handler is recorded and counted but cannot fault the kernel (the tick is committed).
153	- **(b) Completion sentinel.** The kernel arms `ctx.completed = false` and a fresh `ctx.token` before each call; `ctx.complete()` sets `completed` and returns that token — a typed, non-nil, non-zero object (a per-call `CompletionToken` instance) that the kernel compares **by identity**, so a `null`, `0`, `false` or empty value returned by an aborted or forgetful function can never read as success. A call that returns anything but the armed token with `completed` set (the script aborted on an engine error, or forgot) is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` for `apply`, hooks, `validate`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` and `init_world`, and a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic, without a fault, for a P5 or result handler and for `read_view` (which returns an empty view). In a release build the sentinel is the only abort guard (`assert` is compiled out), so it is exercised on a release export in the spike (Acceptance Criteria, KRN-CTX-06). The sentinel catches a *function that aborted*; it cannot catch an error in a nested helper that the outer function then ignores — which is why mutators also return statuses and callers must propagate them.
154	- **(c) What cannot be done.** Engine script errors cannot be intercepted. P5 subscriber isolation is therefore **best-effort plus lint**: the kernel calls handlers one at a time from its own loop, so an aborted handler does not stop the loop; the sentinel names the offending subscriber in diagnostics; a lint forbids handlers from calling anything that can write.
155	- **(d) Violations.** A *violation* (write outside a `WriteScope`, a sim read of `PERCEPTION_OUT`, a hook reaching the `PLAYER` ingress, a submit during `SAVING`, a payload that passed the size check but fails the round-trip, a `SIM` hash change at the tripwire) is, in every build: the offending action refused, a named diagnostics counter incremented, `push_error` called. Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the kernel additionally calls the injected `violation_handler(code, detail)`; the dev default halts via `assert(false)`, the test default records. No state-machine outcome (`FAULTED`, reject reasons, results) differs between profiles.
156	- **(e) KernelProfile.** `KernelProfile` ∈ {`STRICT_DEBUG`, `LENIENT_RELEASE`} is injected at construction (H10) and never read from `OS.is_debug_build()` inside the kernel, so one test process can construct a kernel per profile and exercise both branches. `STRICT_DEBUG` enables only the extras: the per-command serialization round-trip (CR-4), the violation handler, the `SIM` tripwire (CR-12) and the counter test seams.
157	
158	**Velocity rule (gameplay-programmer, adopted as an acceptance criterion).** Adding a new command verb touches at most two files: one handler and one registration line. If the kernel ever makes a feature cost more than that, the layer will be bypassed — which is the exact lapse TD-FEASIBILITY named. Hence: commands are plain data records (no class per verb), state blocks are coarse (one per domain system, not per entity), and replay/undo/rollback/middleware are deferred.

701	## Architecture Principles
702	
703	1. **The simulation is the truth, and it is pure data.** Every gameplay fact lives in a kernel-registered state block owned by exactly one system, built from `RefCounted` objects and packed arrays, with no `Node`, no `Resource` and no scene-tree dependency. It runs headless and is unit-testable. *(Pillar 1; TD-FEASIBILITY risk "graph entangled with the scene tree".)*
704	2. **Every change is a command, and the host is the authority, even in single-player.** Player intent enters only as a plain-data command stamped with its issuer; cross-system writes go only through the owner's published mutators inside a kernel WriteScope. Co-op is a transport added later, not a rewrite. *(TD-FEASIBILITY B2.)*
705	3. **Presentation reads, never writes; perception never reaches the simulation.** Presentation subscribes to change notifications and draws from read views. A hallucination is a presentation-side transform through `perceived()`; `PERCEPTION_OUT` is unreadable from the simulation, and truth channels (trails, real light radius, character sprites, crewmate beams, physical consequences) never pass through the Filter. *(Pillar 4 guard rails; "no lie is unfalsifiable".)*
706	4. **Deterministic by construction.** Fixed 60 Hz integer ticks, integer state, ascending-id iteration, keyed RNG streams with persisted counters, and one hash definition. Same save bytes plus the same restore epoch and command stream give the same state hash. Determinism is what makes replay tests, save verification and later co-op mirroring possible.
707	5. **Versioned, verified persistence from v1.** Saves serialise data models, never scenes; every block carries a schema version migrated by its owner; every file is self-verifying and written atomically; a bad save never faults the kernel and never overwrites a good one. *(TD-FEASIBILITY: "save format not versioned from v1".)*
708	6. **Budgets are measured, not assumed.** Every performance claim is a P99 on a Godot 4.7.2 release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; hot paths allocate nothing per tick; work is bounded by construction (caps and counted work units, never wall-clock), so a budget miss is a tuning change, not a redesign.

## Required ADRs

Thirty-four decisions. Numbers are sequential; the GDD-named candidates each one absorbs are in brackets, so `/architecture-decision` can find the anchors. Several GDD candidates were the same decision under two names and are merged: ADR-LAY-03 and ADR-BODY-03 (scene projection); ADR-BODY-04 and the kernel tick ADR (tick source); ADR-LAY-02 and Emitter candidate 4 (OccluderSource); ADR-LAY-07 belongs to the kernel restore order. **v2 changes:** ADR-0009 is split so the subscriber contract every presentation system needs is Foundation while the Y-sort scene shape (gated by SP-YSORT-1) becomes Core ADR-0034; ADR-0018 folds into ADR-0028 if the lighting spike settles both at once; ADR-0006, ADR-0007 and ADR-0024 carry 64-65 requirements each and are written as sectioned ADRs with one numbered sub-decision per section (container / versioning / restore epoch; content pipeline / boot lints / ids; isolation / Filter query / truth-channel tags) so each part can be reviewed on its own.

### Must have before coding starts (Foundation)

| ADR-0003 | State-block registry, write discipline and owner-callable contract | kernel OQ 7, 10 | RefCounted blocks, owner base class or registered Callables, WriteScope, Class A/B mutators, `ctx.complete()`, the interface types and FAULT_CODE table, hook topo-sort, kernel state machine (incl. OQ-5) |

| ADR-0006 | Save container, generations, versioning and restore epoch | ADR-LSG-05, S-1, rulings R13/R14 | file container, ring, write protocol, worker thread, migration, 64-bit interchange, PROFILE split, `slot_epoch.bin` |

| S1 / SP-ENG-1 (GDScript hot-path cost on an RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK release export: a stub Graph with 12 phases, `emitter.place`, the P3 loop at realistic counts, **accessor and `Callable.call` overhead per ms**, four-tick catch-up; needs an exported benchmark harness outside gdUnit4) | ADR-0012, ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0017; decides the GDExtension rung | graph, layout, body, emitter |

**Spike order** (lead-programmer): S1 first, then the kernel skeleton (KRN-LAT-02), then S0-a/b, then the weld property test, then the save worker. The rendering spikes (pipeline step 11, lighting, SP-YSORT-1) do not depend on the simulation and run in parallel once the first three are under way; the lighting spike must reach its renderer decision before Foundation coding.

---

## Architecture Principles

1. **The simulation is the truth, and it is pure data.** Every gameplay fact lives in a kernel-registered state block owned by exactly one system, built from `RefCounted` objects and packed arrays, with no `Node`, no `Resource` and no scene-tree dependency. It runs headless and is unit-testable. *(Pillar 1; TD-FEASIBILITY risk "graph entangled with the scene tree".)*
2. **Every change is a command, and the host is the authority, even in single-player.** Player intent enters only as a plain-data command stamped with its issuer; cross-system writes go only through the owner's published mutators inside a kernel WriteScope. Co-op is a transport added later, not a rewrite. *(TD-FEASIBILITY B2.)*
3. **Presentation reads, never writes; perception never reaches the simulation.** Presentation subscribes to change notifications and draws from read views. A hallucination is a presentation-side transform through `perceived()`; `PERCEPTION_OUT` is unreadable from the simulation, and truth channels (trails, real light radius, character sprites, crewmate beams, physical consequences) never pass through the Filter. *(Pillar 4 guard rails; "no lie is unfalsifiable".)*
4. **Deterministic by construction.** Fixed 60 Hz integer ticks, integer state, ascending-id iteration, keyed RNG streams with persisted counters, and one hash definition. Same save bytes plus the same restore epoch and command stream give the same state hash. Determinism is what makes replay tests, save verification and later co-op mirroring possible.
5. **Versioned, verified persistence from v1.** Saves serialise data models, never scenes; every block carries a schema version migrated by its owner; every file is self-verifying and written atomically; a bad save never faults the kernel and never overwrites a good one. *(TD-FEASIBILITY: "save format not versioned from v1".)*
6. **Budgets are measured, not assumed.** Every performance claim is a P99 on a Godot 4.7.2 release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; hot paths allocate nothing per tick; work is bounded by construction (caps and counted work units, never wall-clock), so a budget miss is a tuning change, not a redesign.

---

306	### 2. Command path (a player verb)
307	
308	```
309	Adapter (frame N)          Kernel tick T                         Owner
310	  submit("begin_patch",   P1 intake: stamp issuer_peer, origin,
311	   {target}, actor,          seq, submission_id; queued_tick = T-1
312	   correlation)  ───────► P2: origin ∈ allowed_origins?
313	                              actor owned by issuer's PlayerId? ──► Interaction.validate(cmd, views, ctx)
314	                              (Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED) else)       ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason)
315	                                                                 ──► Interaction.apply(cmd, scope, ctx)
316	                                                                       Controller.set_channel_ref(...)
317	                                                                       return ctx.complete()

322	    correlation)

325	The Adapter never predicts an outcome except body motion and sound (pre-play keyed by `correlation`); light and effects change only on committed state.

327	### 3. Weld transaction (cross-system atomic write)
328	
329	```
330	begin_weld (PLAYER) ── validate (static predicates only: can_join_static, socket_plan, docked)
331	   └─ apply: Interaction.open_channel(seat, ASSEMBLY, verb, target, WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS=360)
332	interaction.step × 360 ticks (re-checks lit and reach every LIT_RECHECK_TICKS)
333	assembly.step sees channel DONE ── submit_system("weld", {actor, target, cause})
334	next tick P2: weld.validate (authoritative site; full can_join) ── weld.apply, one WriteScope:
335	   Graph.weld_join (M2) → Layout.attach_section (LM2) → Body.rebase_on_attach (BM3)
336	   → Interaction.sync_section × 2 → assembly.state
337	   each call returns OK or FAULT_CODE; first non-OK → ctx.fault() → kernel FAULTED (no rollback)
338	P5: one notification batch (graph, layout, body, interaction, assembly keys) + BODY_TRANSFER
339	   → PROJECTOR rebuild, Emitter re-derives body_id (W0), Lighting rebuilds occluders, camera rebase
340	Save/Load polls Assembly.last_shape_change_T() → ASSEMBLY_WELD autosave (subject to gates)
341	```
342	
343	Cut is the same shape with M3 → LM3 → BM4; install is a TAP command (Graph `check_install_module` → M5 → Suit `release_carried` → Controller `clear_carry_ref` → `sync_section`).
344	
345	### 4. Event and notification path
346	
347	- **Simulation → presentation:** P5 notification `(block_id, tick, change_keys)` with no state payload. Dirty keys are ints `(KIND << 32) | id`, namespaced per block. Past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` (256) a batch collapses to `ALL`. PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches are merged across a multi-tick frame and delivered once; INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick.
348	- **Presentation → simulation:** only commands through an INPUT_SURFACE handle. There is no other path.
349	- **Simulation → simulation:** synchronous calls inside the tick: pure reads of another block's read view, and published mutators called inside the caller's WriteScope. A cross-block write is always a published mutator of the owning system (Class A checked or Class B clamped). Simulation code never subscribes to notifications (an object that owns a block or hook never subscribes, CR-10).
350	- **P5 events** (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`, …) are notifications that carry no simulation state; Save/Load reads them as autosave triggers.
351	- **Engine signals** are used only inside presentation (e.g. `card_opened`, settings change). The kernel's observer registry is not built on engine signals (decision for ADR-0004).
352	
353	### 5. Perception path (the one place a lie can enter)
354	
355	```
356	Sanity (SIM) ── sanity.drift ──► sanity.perception (PERCEPTION_OUT, per viewer, never persisted)
357	                                        │  (simulation reads of it return empty + violation)
358	Instrument / HUD presenter ── perceived(ref, viewer) ──► Perception Filter
359	                                        │ reads true value (Graph / Suit read view)
360	                                        │ reads sanity.perception entry for (ref, viewer)
361	                                        ▼
362	                               Perceived {displayed_value, motion_mode, leak_amplitude_pm, …}
363	Truth channels never pass through the Filter: Failure & Trail, true reveal radius (Lighting L0),
364	character sprites, crewmate beams, HUD frame, physical consequences in the Graph.
365	```
366	
367	The Graph's `state_hash` is identical with and without perception content; the simulation never computes a perceived value.
368	
369	### 6. Save path
370	
371	```
372	Trigger (interval 10 800 ticks, ASSEMBLY_WELD/CUT, SALVAGE_CUT, QUIT, NEW_GAME)
373	 └─ gates (DOWNED, refractory, suit CRITICAL, owed warning, RAGGED breach) hold or defer ≤ 7 200 ticks
374	Save/Load ── request_snapshot ──► Kernel at P6: SAVING (one boundary service, synchronous, T fixed)
375	   every persist block: snapshot(ctx) → ctx.put(plain data, deep copy, sorted ids)
376	   ◄── payloads split by persist_scope: WORLD → generation, PROFILE → profile.sav
377	Main thread: encode + hand-off ≤ SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS 4 ms
378	Worker thread (immutable PackedByteArrays + paths only):
379	   write .tmp → flush → re-read → re-hash → rotate oldest → rename → verify → campaign.json
380	   any failure: previous generations untouched, save_status FAILED, bounded backoff
381	```
382	
383	### 7. Load / restore path
384	
385	```
386	Continue / death stub ── pre-check (pure: bytes, registry view, build constants; no kernel)
387	   └─ pass: epoch staging (slot_epoch.bin write, polled per frame) → EPOCH_DURABLE

### 2. Command path (a player verb)

```
Adapter (frame N)          Kernel tick T                         Owner
  submit("begin_patch",   P1 intake: stamp issuer_peer, origin,
   {target}, actor,          seq, submission_id; queued_tick = T-1
   correlation)  ───────► P2: origin ∈ allowed_origins?
                              actor owned by issuer's PlayerId? ──► Interaction.validate(cmd, views, ctx)
                              (Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED) else)       ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason)
                                                                 ──► Interaction.apply(cmd, scope, ctx)
                                                                       Controller.set_channel_ref(...)
                                                                       return ctx.complete()
                          P3: interaction.step advances the channel each tick
                          P4 commit ; P5 notify (interaction.state keys)
  result record ◄──────── one terminal result per command (Applied / Rejected(reason) /
   (reason code,            Dropped / Faulted / Superseded), flushed at P5 and once per frame
    correlation)
```

The Adapter never predicts an outcome except body motion and sound (pre-play keyed by `correlation`); light and effects change only on committed state.

### 3. Weld transaction (cross-system atomic write)

```
begin_weld (PLAYER) ── validate (static predicates only: can_join_static, socket_plan, docked)
   └─ apply: Interaction.open_channel(seat, ASSEMBLY, verb, target, WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS=360)
interaction.step × 360 ticks (re-checks lit and reach every LIT_RECHECK_TICKS)
assembly.step sees channel DONE ── submit_system("weld", {actor, target, cause})
next tick P2: weld.validate (authoritative site; full can_join) ── weld.apply, one WriteScope:
   Graph.weld_join (M2) → Layout.attach_section (LM2) → Body.rebase_on_attach (BM3)
   → Interaction.sync_section × 2 → assembly.state
   each call returns OK or FAULT_CODE; first non-OK → ctx.fault() → kernel FAULTED (no rollback)
P5: one notification batch (graph, layout, body, interaction, assembly keys) + BODY_TRANSFER
   → PROJECTOR rebuild, Emitter re-derives body_id (W0), Lighting rebuilds occluders, camera rebase
Save/Load polls Assembly.last_shape_change_T() → ASSEMBLY_WELD autosave (subject to gates)
```

Cut is the same shape with M3 → LM3 → BM4; install is a TAP command (Graph `check_install_module` → M5 → Suit `release_carried` → Controller `clear_carry_ref` → `sync_section`).

### 4. Event and notification path

- **Simulation → presentation:** P5 notification `(block_id, tick, change_keys)` with no state payload. Dirty keys are ints `(KIND << 32) | id`, namespaced per block. Past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` (256) a batch collapses to `ALL`. PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches are merged across a multi-tick frame and delivered once; INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick.
- **Presentation → simulation:** only commands through an INPUT_SURFACE handle. There is no other path.
- **Simulation → simulation:** synchronous calls inside the tick: pure reads of another block's read view, and published mutators called inside the caller's WriteScope. A cross-block write is always a published mutator of the owning system (Class A checked or Class B clamped). Simulation code never subscribes to notifications (an object that owns a block or hook never subscribes, CR-10).
- **P5 events** (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`, …) are notifications that carry no simulation state; Save/Load reads them as autosave triggers.
- **Engine signals** are used only inside presentation (e.g. `card_opened`, settings change). The kernel's observer registry is not built on engine signals (decision for ADR-0004).

### 5. Perception path (the one place a lie can enter)

```
Sanity (SIM) ── sanity.drift ──► sanity.perception (PERCEPTION_OUT, per viewer, never persisted)
                                        │  (simulation reads of it return empty + violation)
Instrument / HUD presenter ── perceived(ref, viewer) ──► Perception Filter
                                        │ reads true value (Graph / Suit read view)
                                        │ reads sanity.perception entry for (ref, viewer)
                                        ▼
                               Perceived {displayed_value, motion_mode, leak_amplitude_pm, …}
Truth channels never pass through the Filter: Failure & Trail, true reveal radius (Lighting L0),
character sprites, crewmate beams, HUD frame, physical consequences in the Graph.
```

The Graph's `state_hash` is identical with and without perception content; the simulation never computes a perceived value.

### 6. Save path

```
Trigger (interval 10 800 ticks, ASSEMBLY_WELD/CUT, SALVAGE_CUT, QUIT, NEW_GAME)
 └─ gates (DOWNED, refractory, suit CRITICAL, owed warning, RAGGED breach) hold or defer ≤ 7 200 ticks
Save/Load ── request_snapshot ──► Kernel at P6: SAVING (one boundary service, synchronous, T fixed)
   every persist block: snapshot(ctx) → ctx.put(plain data, deep copy, sorted ids)
   ◄── payloads split by persist_scope: WORLD → generation, PROFILE → profile.sav
Main thread: encode + hand-off ≤ SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS 4 ms
Worker thread (immutable PackedByteArrays + paths only):
   write .tmp → flush → re-read → re-hash → rotate oldest → rename → verify → campaign.json
   any failure: previous generations untouched, save_status FAILED, bounded backoff
```

### 7. Load / restore path

```
Continue / death stub ── pre-check (pure: bytes, registry view, build constants; no kernel)
   └─ pass: epoch staging (slot_epoch.bin write, polled per frame) → EPOCH_DURABLE
      (or SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE, save_status FAILED, restore proceeds — listed exposure, R14)
Kernel request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash) at P6: LOADING (one boundary service)
   restore each WORLD block in restore_after order (two-phase: decode+validate into scratch, then swap)
   post_restore each block in the same order (derived caches, cross-block verification)
   rebuild binding table half (b) from binding sources (seat_bindings, beam_bindings)
   reproduction check: state_hash vs header (reported, never a fallback reason)
   → RUNNING; accumulator cleared; camera CUT; Adapter resends intents; first frame passes through the Filter
```

**restore_after order (MVP):** `layout.state` → `graph.state` → `body.state` → `controller.state` → `emitter.state`, `suit.state` → `interaction.state` → `assembly.state`, `web.state`; then Attention, Horror and Sanity (their restore_after lists are in their GDDs; the kernel topo-sorts the declared DAG).

**Threading.** Exactly one thread boundary exists in the MVP: the save writer (and its read-back). Everything else, kernel, owner callables and presentation, runs on the main thread; `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` and `call_deferred` into kernel code are lint-forbidden (CR-1a).

### 8. Initialisation order

```
1. Engine boot; project.godot guard rails asserted (stretch, filters, snap, hdr_2d, physics_interpolation off)
2. Pipeline root builds the viewport stack (BOOTING → PRESENTING)
3. Content data loads in a fixed order: Item DB → section templates (manifest order) → world records,
   verb tables, tuning tables; boot lints and invariant assertions (refuse the build on failure)
4. Kernel BOOTING: owners register blocks, command types, hooks, binding sources, diagnostics channels
   (Layout, Graph last of the Item DB → Layout → Graph chain; then Body, Controller, Emitter, Suit,
   Interaction, Assembly, Web, Attention, Horror, Sanity). Registration then freezes; hook topo-sort.
5. Presentation subscribers subscribe (Lighting, Trail, HUD, Instruments, Audio, PROJECTORs, Debug)
6. Main menu (Chart Table) → New Game: Save/Load new_game(seed) → kernel request_new_game(seed, 0)
   → Web Map init_world inside one WriteScope: Layout build_section → Emitter instantiate_section_emitters
   → Interaction sync_section → PROJECTOR notification → initial NEW_GAME generation written
   or Continue: load path (§ 7)
```

---

## API Boundaries

Signatures are GDScript (typed). They restate the GDD contracts at the boundary; the GDD anchor in brackets is the authority.

		after: Array[StringName], tolerates_stale: Array[StringName]) -> void

# Docs Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## Architecture Decision Records (`docs/architecture/`)

Use the ADR template: `.claude/docs/templates/architecture-decision-record.md`

**Required sections:** Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences,
ADR Dependencies, Engine Compatibility, GDD Requirements Addressed

**Status lifecycle:** `Proposed` → `Accepted` → `Superseded`
- Never skip `Accepted` — stories referencing a `Proposed` ADR are auto-blocked
- Use `/architecture-decision` to create ADRs through the guided flow

**TR Registry:** `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`
- Stable requirement IDs (e.g. `TR-movement-001`) that link GDD requirements to stories
- Never renumber existing IDs — only append new ones
- Updated by `/architecture-review` Phase 8

**Control Manifest:** `docs/architecture/control-manifest.md`
- Flat programmer rules sheet: Required / Forbidden / Guardrails per layer
- Date-stamped `Manifest Version:` in header
- Stories embed this version; `/story-done` checks for staleness

**Validation:** Run `/architecture-review` after completing a set of ADRs.

## Engine Reference (`docs/engine-reference/`)

Version-pinned engine API snapshots. **Always check here before using any
engine API** — the LLM's training data predates the pinned engine version.

Current engine: see `docs/engine-reference/<engine>/VERSION.md` (`<engine>` is `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`, matching `engine.name` in `project.yaml`)

The rendering spikes (pipeline step 11, lighting, SP-YSORT-1) do not depend on the simulation and run in parallel once the first three are under way; the lighting spike must reach its renderer decision before Foundation coding.
698	
699	---
700	
701	## Architecture Principles
702	
703	1. **The simulation is the truth, and it is pure data.** Every gameplay fact lives in a kernel-registered state block owned by exactly one system, built from `RefCounted` objects and packed arrays, with no `Node`, no `Resource` and no scene-tree dependency. It runs headless and is unit-testable. *(Pillar 1; TD-FEASIBILITY risk "graph entangled with the scene tree".)*
704	2. **Every change is a command, and the host is the authority, even in single-player.** Player intent enters only as a plain-data command stamped with its issuer; cross-system writes go only through the owner's published mutators inside a kernel WriteScope. Co-op is a transport added later, not a rewrite. *(TD-FEASIBILITY B2.)*
705	3. **Presentation reads, never writes; perception never reaches the simulation.** Presentation subscribes to change notifications and draws from read views. A hallucination is a presentation-side transform through `perceived()`; `PERCEPTION_OUT` is unreadable from the simulation, and truth channels (trails, real light radius, character sprites, crewmate beams, physical consequences) never pass through the Filter. *(Pillar 4 guard rails; "no lie is unfalsifiable".)*
706	4. **Deterministic by construction.** Fixed 60 Hz integer ticks, integer state, ascending-id iteration, keyed RNG streams with persisted counters, and one hash definition. Same save bytes plus the same restore epoch and command stream give the same state hash. Determinism is what makes replay tests, save verification and later co-op mirroring possible.
707	5. **Versioned, verified persistence from v1.** Saves serialise data models, never scenes; every block carries a schema version migrated by its owner; every file is self-verifying and written atomically; a bad save never faults the kernel and never overwrites a good one. *(TD-FEASIBILITY: "save format not versioned from v1".)*
708	6. **Budgets are measured, not assumed.** Every performance claim is a P99 on a Godot 4.7.2 release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; hot paths allocate nothing per tick; work is bounded by construction (caps and counted work units, never wall-clock), so a budget miss is a tuning change, not a redesign.
709	
710	---

733	### Cross-GDD inconsistencies found while building the baseline
734	
735	These came out of mapping the 794 requirements to ADRs. They are stated as the extracted requirements state them; check the GDD text before fixing. Each is small, and none changes a layer or an ownership decision above. The owner (rule G1) is named where one is clear.

306	### 2. Command path (a player verb)
307	
308	```
309	Adapter (frame N)          Kernel tick T                         Owner
310	  submit("begin_patch",   P1 intake: stamp issuer_peer, origin,
311	   {target}, actor,          seq, submission_id; queued_tick = T-1
312	   correlation)  ───────► P2: origin ∈ allowed_origins?
313	                              actor owned by issuer's PlayerId? ──► Interaction.validate(cmd, views, ctx)
314	                              (Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED) else)       ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason)
315	                                                                 ──► Interaction.apply(cmd, scope, ctx)
316	                                                                       Controller.set_channel_ref(...)
317	                                                                       return ctx.complete()
318	                          P3: interaction.step advances the channel each tick
319	                          P4 commit ; P5 notify (interaction.state keys)
320	  result record ◄──────── one terminal result per command (Applied / Rejected(reason) /
321	   (reason code,            Dropped / Faulted / Superseded), flushed at P5 and once per frame
322	    correlation)
323	```
324	
325	The Adapter never predicts an outcome except body motion and sound (pre-play keyed by `correlation`); light and effects change only on committed state.
326	
327	### 3. Weld transaction (cross-system atomic write)
328	
329	```
330	begin_weld (PLAYER) ── validate (static predicates only: can_join_static, socket_plan, docked)
331	   └─ apply: Interaction.open_channel(seat, ASSEMBLY, verb, target, WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS=360)
332	interaction.step × 360 ticks (re-checks lit and reach every LIT_RECHECK_TICKS)
333	assembly.step sees channel DONE ── submit_system("weld", {actor, target, cause})
334	next tick P2: weld.validate (authoritative site; full can_join) ── weld.apply, one WriteScope:
335	   Graph.weld_join (M2) → Layout.attach_section (LM2) → Body.rebase_on_attach (BM3)
336	   → Interaction.sync_section × 2 → assembly.state
337	   each call returns OK or FAULT_CODE; first non-OK → ctx.fault() → kernel FAULTED (no rollback)
338	P5: one notification batch (graph, layout, body, interaction, assembly keys) + BODY_TRANSFER
339	   → PROJECTOR rebuild, Emitter re-derives body_id (W0), Lighting rebuilds occluders, camera rebase
340	Save/Load polls Assembly.last_shape_change_T() → ASSEMBLY_WELD autosave (subject to gates)
341	```
342	
343	Cut is the same shape with M3 → LM3 → BM4; install is a TAP command (Graph `check_install_module` → M5 → Suit `release_carried` → Controller `clear_carry_ref` → `sync_section`).
344	
345	### 4. Event and notification path
346	
347	- **Simulation → presentation:** P5 notification `(block_id, tick, change_keys)` with no state payload. Dirty keys are ints `(KIND << 32) | id`, namespaced per block. Past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` (256) a batch collapses to `ALL`. PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches are merged across a multi-tick frame and delivered once; INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick.
348	- **Presentation → simulation:** only commands through an INPUT_SURFACE handle. There is no other path.
349	- **Simulation → simulation:** synchronous calls inside the tick: pure reads of another block's read view, and published mutators called inside the caller's WriteScope. A cross-block write is always a published mutator of the owning system (Class A checked or Class B clamped). Simulation code never subscribes to notifications (an object that owns a block or hook never subscribes, CR-10).
350	- **P5 events** (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`, …) are notifications that carry no simulation state; Save/Load reads them as autosave triggers.
351	- **Engine signals** are used only inside presentation (e.g. `card_opened`, settings change). The kernel's observer registry is not built on engine signals (decision for ADR-0004).
352	
353	### 5. Perception path (the one place a lie can enter)
354	
355	```
356	Sanity (SIM) ── sanity.drift ──► sanity.perception (PERCEPTION_OUT, per viewer, never persisted)
357	                                        │  (simulation reads of it return empty + violation)
358	Instrument / HUD presenter ── perceived(ref, viewer) ──► Perception Filter
359	                                        │ reads true value (Graph / Suit read view)
360	                                        │ reads sanity.perception entry for (ref, viewer)
361	                                        ▼
362	                               Perceived {displayed_value, motion_mode, leak_amplitude_pm, …}
363	Truth channels never pass through the Filter: Failure & Trail, true reveal radius (Lighting L0),
364	character sprites, crewmate beams, HUD frame, physical consequences in the Graph.
365	```
366	
367	The Graph's `state_hash` is identical with and without perception content; the simulation never computes a perceived value.
368	
369	### 6. Save path
370	
371	```
372	Trigger (interval 10 800 ticks, ASSEMBLY_WELD/CUT, SALVAGE_CUT, QUIT, NEW_GAME)
373	 └─ gates (DOWNED, refractory, suit CRITICAL, owed warning, RAGGED breach) hold or defer ≤ 7 200 ticks
374	Save/Load ── request_snapshot ──► Kernel at P6: SAVING (one boundary service, synchronous, T fixed)
375	   every persist block: snapshot(ctx) → ctx.put(plain data, deep copy, sorted ids)
376	   ◄── payloads split by persist_scope: WORLD → generation, PROFILE → profile.sav
377	Main thread: encode + hand-off ≤ SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS 4 ms
378	Worker thread (immutable PackedByteArrays + paths only):
379	   write .tmp → flush → re-read → re-hash → rotate oldest → rename → verify → campaign.json
380	   any failure: previous generations untouched, save_status FAILED, bounded backoff
381	```
382	
383	### 7. Load / restore path
384	
385	```
386	Continue / death stub ── pre-check (pure: bytes, registry view, build constants; no kernel)
387	   └─ pass: epoch staging (slot_epoch.bin write, polled per frame) → EPOCH_DURABLE
388	      (or SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE, save_status FAILED, restore proceeds — listed exposure, R14)
389	Kernel request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash) at P6: LOADING (one boundary service)
390	   restore each WORLD block in restore_after order (two-phase: decode+validate into scratch, then swap)
391	   post_restore each block in the same order (derived caches, cross-block verification)
392	   rebuild binding table half (b) from binding sources (seat_bindings, beam_bindings)
393	   reproduction check: state_hash vs header (reported, never a fallback reason)
394	   → RUNNING; accumulator cleared; camera CUT; Adapter resends intents; first frame passes through the Filter
395	```
396	
397	**restore_after order (MVP):** `layout.state` → `graph.state` → `body.state` → `controller.state` → `emitter.state`, `suit.state` → `interaction.state` → `assembly.state`, `web.state`; then Attention, Horror and Sanity (their restore_after lists are in their GDDs; the kernel topo-sorts the declared DAG).
398	
399	**Threading.** Exactly one thread boundary exists in the MVP: the save writer (and its read-back). Everything else, kernel, owner callables and presentation, runs on the main thread; `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` and `call_deferred` into kernel code are lint-forbidden (CR-1a).
400	
401	### 8. Initialisation order
402	
403	```
404	1. Engine boot; project.godot guard rails asserted (stretch, filters, snap, hdr_2d, physics_interpolation off)
405	2. Pipeline root builds the viewport stack (BOOTING → PRESENTING)
406	3. Content data loads in a fixed order: Item DB → section templates (manifest order) → world records,
407	   verb tables, tuning tables; boot lints and invariant assertions (refuse the build on failure)
408	4. Kernel BOOTING: owners register blocks, command types, hooks, binding sources, diagnostics channels
409	   (Layout, Graph last of the Item DB → Layout → Graph chain; then Body, Controller, Emitter, Suit,
410	   Interaction, Assembly, Web, Attention, Horror, Sanity). Registration then freezes; hook topo-sort.
411	5. Presentation subscribers subscribe (Lighting, Trail, HUD, Instruments, Audio, PROJECTORs, Debug)
412	6. Main menu (Chart Table) → New Game: Save/Load new_game(seed) → kernel request_new_game(seed, 0)
413	   → Web Map init_world inside one WriteScope: Layout build_section → Emitter instantiate_section_emitters
414	   → Interaction sync_section → PROJECTOR notification → initial NEW_GAME generation written
415	   or Continue: load path (§ 7)
416	```
417	
418	---
419	
420	## API Boundaries
421	
422	Signatures are GDScript (typed). They restate the GDD contracts at the boundary; the GDD anchor in brackets is the authority.
423	
424	### Kernel ingress and registration [command-simulation-layer CR-4..CR-10, CR-19]
425	
426	```gdscript
427	# Ingress (INPUT_SURFACE handle only). Fire-and-forget: returns nothing, calls nothing.
428	func submit(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, actor: int = NO_ACTOR, correlation: int = 0) -> void
429	# SYSTEM-origin submission from a step hook or apply (dedupe optional).
430	func submit_system(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> void
431	
432	# Registration — legal only in BOOTING, frozen afterwards; violations fail boot.
433	func register_block(desc: BlockDescriptor) -> void       # block_id, owner, schema_version, class, persist,
434	                                                          # persist_scope, scope, gameplay, interpolated,
435	                                                          # repl_hint, restore_after, callables
436	func register_command(desc: CommandTypeDescriptor) -> void  # allowed_origins, actor_binding, actor_source,
437	                                                          # coalesce, max_age_ticks, allowed_when_paused, writes_blocks
438	func register_hook(hook_id: StringName, owner: Object, divisor: int, offset: int,
439			after: Array[StringName], tolerates_stale: Array[StringName]) -> void
440	func subscribe(cls: SubscriberClass, handler: Callable) -> SubscriptionHandle
441	```
442	
443	**Invariants callers respect:** never construct a command with `issuer_peer`; payloads hold only whitelisted Variant types (finite floats, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 4 KiB, no Object/Callable/NodePath/RID); never submit from a PRESENTATION handler. **Kernel guarantees:** exactly one terminal result per command; apply order ascending `(queued_tick, host_order)`; subscribers see only post-P4 state.
444	
445	### Owner-callable contract [CR-19, ruling R3]
